C-VNEXT-ARCHITECTURE-DECISION-20260906.Summary: Convert the Astra audit recommendation into an approved Worldline vNext architecture decision: portable product, feature, capability, state, and UI models above substantially engine-specific runtimes, with Chromium and CEF as the first desktop assembly.
C-VNEXT-ARCHITECTURE-DECISION-20260906.Problem: The current accepted invariants correctly prevent product policy from entering the kernel, but they do not distinguish ordinary replaceable features from mandatory security-critical system components. Existing engine-neutral contracts can also be misread as a promise of Chromium and Firefox parity even though no Gecko runtime exists. The project needs a durable decision defining the trusted core, the wider TCB, portability boundary, engine profiles, version domains, and authority unavailable to generated code.

Goals.Goal: Accept or explicitly supersede ADR-WORLDLINE-VNEXT with strategy C and CEF-first implementation.
Define the minimal control kernel separately from the full trusted computing base.
Clarify that mandatory system brokers and protected recovery and UI components may be required by boot policy without receiving hidden product-role authority.
Define portable capability, feature, UI, state, and typed-outcome contracts plus negotiated engine-specific operation profiles and extensions.
Define independent version domains for product release, package, manifest schema, feature ABI, capability contract, engine profile, state schema, and native IPC.
Freeze architectural invariants that AI agents and generated features cannot change through ordinary feature authority.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL DOES NOT APPROVE A PLAN OR IMPLEMENTATION.
C-VNEXT-RUNTIME-TRUTH-RECONCILIATION-20260906 must be approved and applied before this change is planned.
The kernel remains free of browser, model, provider, workspace, and UI domain policy.
Trust class comes from verified installation and boot policy, never from plugin name, product role, signature alone, or AI authorship.
Unsupported engine guarantees fail explicitly; security-sensitive downgrade or silent no-op behavior is forbidden.
CEF, CDP, Gecko, native pointers, raw profile paths, and engine database schemas must not enter the portable feature ABI.
Firefox parity is not a current product commitment and no Gecko implementation is authorized by this change.
Ordinary user or AI features cannot replace authorization, credential, updater, consent, origin-indicator, stop, or recovery mechanisms.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Implementing the feature host, sandbox, package loader, brokers, or UI runtime.
Selecting a desktop Gecko embedding technology.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: An accepted ADR states that Worldline uses a portable product model with engine-specific runtimes and names Chromium and CEF as the first desktop runtime.
The ADR distinguishes the small generic kernel from the complete TCB, including OS, engine privileged process, FFI, Wasmtime host, mandatory brokers, protected UI, updater, and recovery launcher.
The kernel invariant is clarified so product role never grants privilege while verified mandatory system components can be required by boot composition.
A capability taxonomy distinguishes portable operations, engine-profile operations, engine-specific extensions, system-only capabilities, and explicitly forbidden ordinary-feature capabilities.
Operation negotiation returns an explicit support profile and cannot advertise an operation whose selected backend returns unconditional Unsupported.
All version domains and their compatibility or fail-closed rules are listed independently.

Generated code is explicitly denied raw native execution, arbitrary process spawn, ambient filesystem and network access, credential export, updater control, sandbox control, and direct engine debugging by default.
A Gecko decision gate requires demonstrated product demand, supported embedding, update ownership, isolation evidence, and bounded investment before implementation.
Follow-on changes have explicit dependency order and do not inherit approval from this architecture decision.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The accepted ADR, roadmap, module projections, capability vocabulary, and executable architecture checks agree on strategy C, kernel purity, explicit engine profiles, fail-closed unsupported operations, and protected system authority.

Assumptions.Assumption: The reconciliation package confirms the audit findings and current CEF-first runtime facts.
A narrow portable layer remains valuable even when individual features require an engine-specific profile.
Existing accepted ADRs can be retained where compatible and explicitly superseded or narrowed where they overstate current reality.
